# What version 3.0 did about the audit

Emitted from `tools/audit_register.py`, so it cannot drift from the register the audit page shows.

v3.0 answered the audit directly, in §30.18. Of 76 items, **18 are fixed in the design document itself**, 17 moved without being resolved, and 12 are new. Six of the new ones came from reading v3.0 the way v2.3 was read; three came from building the harnesses §19.27 now depends on and running them.

## Fixed in v3.0

| | What it was | What v3.0 did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C1** | Two incompatible detection models | §12.8 now says sight and awareness are “specified once, in 12.17” and that the older single-cone, percent-per-second rules are gone. The residue is tracked as C21: §29.1 still tabulates the deleted model, and cites §12.8 for it. |
| **C4** | The master inflation dial is keyed to a level range that does not exist | §9.6’s base is now B(V) with V stated as “the target’s Vault level, one to ten — not the realm level, which stops at five”. One paragraph deeper, §9.6’s what is exposed still says the sealed share runs “40% at realm level 1” while §9.4 says Vault level 1. |
| **C5** | Two defence budget systems, with three different ward limits | §13.4 keeps the slot limits and drops the second pool in as many words: “The older per-realm pool is gone, and these numbers now match 5.2 and 10.2 rather than competing with them.” |
| **D14** | Chords should require three laws, not three notes | §8.8 changes the rule to three distinct laws, which makes §8.5 true. It did not achieve what it argued for: the cheapest chord now costs 33 stability against a day-2 capacity of 51, up from 26, and seven of twelve are still three commons. The gate that actually makes a chord late-game is the Lab level 3 at Spire 5, about day 42 — which §8.5 mentions and §8.8 does not lean on. |
| **F1** | The roster cannot staff the universe the rules permit | §5.9 decides it: one producer of each kind per realm, partial staffing paying pro-rata, and “the roster can never fill everything — 38 ruleborn against far more positions — and that is the scarcity the design is built on”. Scarcity is now a feature by decision rather than by accident. |
| **F2** | Building the second producer doubles income and breaks every pacing date | §5.9: one, not two, with the model’s reasoning quoted. The published tables in §9.3 were not regenerated against it — C19. |
| **F3** | The core trade-off the design is built on does not bind | §5.9: “A crew on a heist is assigned to it, like a guard at a post, and does not work while assigned. Five of thirty-eight is a real choice.” This is the mechanism the finding recommended, taken whole. |
| **F4** | §12.8’s knockout rule is true for three of twenty-five role pairings | §12.8 now reads “triple Power, or half the guard’s full health, whichever is greater”, and says why: the rule below it was true for three of twenty-five pairings without it. Verified — 25 of 25 now. §29.1 still gives triple damage with no floor (C21). |
| **F5** | The Vault’s loading phase lasts two seconds and 46% of crew capacity is unreachable | §12.19. Loading is ten seconds, every role loads, and the fill fraction is a term in §9.6’s formula. The check retires — all 560 units of crew capacity are now reachable. |
| **G1** | Pathfinding and crew movement | §12.18 settles it, and adopts the reading in spec/movement.md: tiles for terrain and building, continuous millitile position and facing, breadth-first pathfinding with a fixed neighbour order, the command recorded rather than the path, and crew passing through one another. The rule that protects premise 3 is stated as a heading: the crew never makes a decision the player did not make. |
| **G2** | What happens when a guard catches you | §12.20, with §12.8 rewritten around it. One hit per 0.8 s for Power damage on both sides; fighting allowed but an unambushed hit sends suspicion straight to 1000; ten seconds down, revived in 3 s or 1.5 s by a Mender; loot dropped on the tile. §29.1 was not updated — C21. |
| **G4** | The Vault's loading loop has no relationship to the payout | §12.19, adopting spec/vault.md whole: every role loads at 30 units a second, a crew fills in ten seconds, the haul is multiplied by the share of bags filled, and the break-even sits at 70%. §9.6 carries the new fill term. §12.6 still says 150 a second — C22. |
| **G6** | How the matchmaking rating actually combines its inputs | §12.22 gives the five steps: the band, the Bayesian rating with its uncertainty term, the guarantee that the median offered target sits in the 55–70% band, the widening order when nothing matches, and why the 0.25 payout tier is unreachable through normal matchmaking. |
| **G8** | Two offline edge cases named but not resolved | §24.13 answers both: one lease per target per player, so a second device is handed the lease the first holds; and the entry fee is debited at validation rather than at lease, so an offline heist never submitted costs nothing. |
| **G9** | The 60-second guided build is the top risk's mitigation and is unspecified | Resolved by removal rather than specification. §13.3 is now “Nobody has to build”: every player has a generated defence from the first minute, curation is the default creative act and authoring is the deep end. The 60-second guided build is no longer the mitigation for risk #1, because the risk is designed out instead of tested. See D20. |
| **Q1** | Is character scarcity a feature or an accident? | Answered by §5.9: scarcity is a feature. |
| **Q2** | Should the raid-versus-build trade-off be made real, or dropped? | Answered by §5.9: crew membership excludes work, so the trade-off binds. |
| **Q4** | One producer per realm, or two? | Answered by §5.9: one producer of each kind per realm. |

| **C2** | Two incompatible raid-payout models, differing by 16–30× | Half resolved. §9.4’s percentages are deleted — “the percentages this paragraph used to carry are gone” — and §9.6 is the one formula, now with a fill term. But §9.6 keeps B(V) rather than pegging to production, so the faucet still delivers 1–2% of income, while §9.4’s balance target (“a fifth of a day’s production… roughly a third”) and §12.1’s 40% are unchanged. The two-model contradiction is gone; the model-versus-target one is not. |

Twelve laws were re-tagged from Rare to Uncommon, so the sheets now read 18/12/6/12 — against §7.10’s own table of 18/14/10/6. Deep doubled from 6 to 12. And §7.6, §14.4 and the glossary still price three ranks at 15/30/60 pages (C23). |

The decision was taken and the second copy was not retired. |

## The shape of it

§30.18 draws the right conclusion from the v2.3 audit: *"a table that exists only to summarise something else should be generated, never authored — four of the six conflicts had no other cause."*

v3.0 then fixed six systems and left a stale copy of four of them. `tools/check_design_consistency.py` has a **Supersession** section that names each one and the exact sentence still carrying the old version; it fails until they are gone. The sharpest case is §29.1, the formulas appendix: it still tabulates the detection model §12.8 deleted, and cites §12.8 as its source.

This file is generated for that reason.
